statements.quote: This writing task is adapted from team collaboration tasks designed in prior literature (Noy and Zhang, 2023).

Before starting each task, every team was first given basic information about the hypothesized product and writing instructions (see the Supplementary material Section 1 for Writing Tasks Instructions).
statements.locator: p. 6, Section 3.3 (Writing task design), reference to Supplementary material Section 1.

statements.quote: Detailed instructions, including sample submissions with high and low scores, can be found in Section 2 in the Supplementary material.
statements.locator: pp. 6-7, Section 3.4.2.1 (Task quality), sentence crossing the page break; reference to Supplementary material Section 2.

statements.quote: Team interaction behaviors were coded using Bales’ Interaction Process Analysis (IPA) framework, which includes 12 subcategories grouped into four functional areas: positive socio-emotional, negative socio-emotional, task-related answering, and task-related questioning (see Section 3 in the Supplementary material).
statements.locator: p. 7, Section 3.4.4 (Team interaction process), reference to Supplementary material Section 3.

notes: Checked on 2026-10-10. Read the complete saved markdown (91631 characters, 819 lines) covering all 16 PDF pages, including end matter and references; checked PDF pages 6, 7, and 14 with PyMuPDF and inspected the PDF hyperlink annotations. The PDF ends with references and has no appended supplement. The public supplementary DOCX was subsequently read in full in memory, including all 92 document paragraphs and the IPA table, with other document parts checked. Quotations normalize physical line/page breaks; the supplementary URL's PDF line wrap is removed. The screening form's data_and_code fields contain no URLs. No code-release or preregistration statement or repository link appears in the saved paper. The data-availability statement promises raw data from the authors, 'without undue reservation', rather than providing a public data location. status=on_request represents this author-mediated availability; the statement does not literally use the words 'on request', and no author was contacted. Only the same materials-only supplement was found at Frontiers and Figshare; none of the title/author API searches identified an additional relevant dataset. The two deposit entries represent one unique DOCX. Isolated illustrative utterances are not a usable output-level corpus, so they do not justify public_partial or public_participant_data. No confirmed participant-data rows or columns were available to inspect. None of the missing numerical statistics in final.open_items can be computed from the public material: unambiguous arm SDs/SEs (item 1), OLS standard errors/variance estimation (item 2), and the PROCESS-versus-OLS row structure and repeated-team handling (item 3) remain unresolved. Arm-specific analyzed participant counts, participant-level scores, and diversity measures from a complete ID-linked text corpus also cannot be recovered. The supplement partly resolves open item 4 by exposing the qualitative rubric and coding examples: the originality prompt is 'Are the ideas presented original and creative?' It contains no numerical originality construction rule, no scored high/low submission examples, and no additional model statistics. The task-length discrepancy is detailed in deposit notes. Sample overlap with DOI 10.1002/pra2.1437 (open item 5) is not established by these materials. S1 randomizes teams and measures team outputs/discussions; such outcomes must not be treated as independent person-level observations. All external calls used urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without credentials or personal identifiers; no access request was made, and downloaded content was kept in memory.
